component_scope_limits: The selected headward and much of the upper route are mapped as Whisky Chitto Creek; the 2010 LDEQ prose spells it Whiskey Chitto Creek. This tributary is not renamed Calcasieu River.
The named Calcasieu River enters from a separate upstream branch at the Whisky Chitto confluence north of US 190. Its own remote headwaters are not the headward end of this selected object.

The lower route includes the connected Lake Charles, Prien Lake and Moss Lake setting, Calcasieu Ship Channel alongside Calcasieu Lake, and the Calcasieu Pass coastal outlet. Their names are not replaced by a single river label.

No exact official source point, exhaustive minor-channel inventory, legal naming status, official length or every-reach scalar identity is established. The retained 207.579 km is model-rendered metadata.

records.region: Río Negro, Argentina; Somuncurá feeder–Yaminué–El Toro wetland belt–Nahuel Niyeu to Laguna Tres Picos.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative identity supported by the labeled lower receiving drainage. It does not uniformly name the unnamed upland feeder, Yaminué canyon and stream, El Toro wetland passage or Tres Picos saline-lagoon interior.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected drainage corresponds to an unnamed Somuncurá upland feeder, Cañadón de Yaminué and the mapped Arroyo Seco Yaminué / Arroyo Yaminué corridor, the El Toro wetland connection, and lower Arroyo Nahuel Niyeu, terminating inside Laguna Tres Picos in Bajo de Valcheta. Arroyo Nahuel Niyeu is supported as the representative lower-system identity, with all upstream and lagoon naming limits retained.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity supported by the labeled lower receiving drainage. It does not uniformly name the unnamed upland feeder, Yaminué canyon and stream, El Toro wetland passage or Tres Picos saline-lagoon interior.

component_scope_limits: The unnamed southeastern upland feeder retains a null hydronym; no representative name is applied to it.
Cañadón de Yaminué is a canyon name; A° Seco Yaminué and A° Yaminué are distinct mapped upstream stream labels.
El Toro and the lower wetland passages are component waterbody settings, not proof of a continuous uniformly named open river.
Arroyo Nahuel Niyeu is the supported lower receiving-river representative, not a formally verified whole-feature registry name.
Laguna Tres Picos is the actual selected terminal. Laguna Indio Muerto is adjacent and also gives its name to the broader basin in the provincial plan.
Historical cartography and historical station observations do not establish current perennial flow, exact source tips, banks or lagoon shorelines.
No Korean name, accepted scalar name or product change is proposed.

records.region: Paraíba and Rio Grande do Norte, Brazil; Pocinhos feeder–Catolé–Curimataú, Cacimba da Várzea reservoir and Barra do Cunhaú coastal setting.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The full selected FID has bounded original-map correspondence to an unnamed northern Pocinhos feeder, the Riacho Catolé connection and the Rio Curimataú receiving corridor. The route passes small upper impounded waters, continues north across the Sapo/Jacinto and Barra do Urubu settings, turns east through Açude Cacimba da Várzea, and follows the connected middle river toward Caiçara. It continues via Nova Cruz and Pedro Velho to lower Curimataú estuarine waters and the Atlantic coastal setting by Barra do Cunhaú. Rio Curimataú is the representative system candidate; the distinct headward label, water bodies and terminal generalization remain component-specific. No material source/connector interval remains unresolved.
